author: Gmelin, 1788

months.note: 1년 내내 볼 수 있다. 4~6월에 큰키나무 줄기에 뚫은 구멍에 알을 낳는다.

summary: 회색 머리와 녹색 몸을 지닌 딱다구리로, 숲에 사는 비교적 흔한 텃새다. 대개 혼자 지내며, 단단한 꼬리깃으로 몸을 받친 채 나무줄기에 곧게 붙거나 줄기를 빙 돌며 위로 올라간다. 곤충을 주로 먹고 그 가운데 개미를 특히 즐기며, 큰키나무 줄기에 구멍을 뚫어 둥지를 만든다.

sexes.female: 머리에 붉은색이 없고, 회색 정수리에 가는 검은 세로 얼룩이 있다.

similar.how: 같은 숲에 흔하지만 몸이 흑백 무늬이고 아랫배와 아래꼬리덮깃이 붉어, 녹색과 회색으로 된 청딱다구리와 쉽게 구별된다.

art.subject: Grey-headed Woodpecker (Picus canus), adult male, as seen in Korean forest in late autumn: head and neck plain ash-grey with a small glossy red patch on the forecrown; narrow black lores and a thin black moustachial stripe; usually fine black streaks on the grey hindcrown; back, scapulars and wing coverts olive-green; rump and uppertail coverts yellowish-green; flight feathers dark brown with rows of whitish spots; tail dark greyish-brown; underparts plain greenish-grey without spots or bars. Bill grey, darker at the tip. Legs dark greenish-grey.
art.pose: clinging upright to a large tree trunk, braced on its stiff tail, head turned in profile
art.scene: Korean mixed deciduous forest in late autumn, thick old trunks, golden and russet leaves, an ant mound at the foot of a tree, soft low sunlight; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male, clinging upright to a trunk, side view: plain grey head with a small red forecrown patch, black lores and thin black moustache, olive-green back and wings, yellowish-green rump, plain greenish-grey underparts
adult female, clinging upright to a trunk, side view: no red on the head, grey crown finely streaked black, thin black moustache, olive-green back, plain greenish-grey underparts
art.build: Medium-sized green woodpecker, 25–26cm, about the length of a Brown-eared Bulbul, slimmer-necked and rounder-headed than the pied woodpeckers. Bill straight, chisel-tipped, relatively slim, about as long as the head. Legs short, greenish-grey, two toes forward and two back; clings to trunks braced on a stiff, pointed tail and also feeds on the ground at ant nests. Wings olive with spotted-barred flight feathers; in flight the yellowish-green rump shows clearly. Flight deeply undulating.
avoid: Do not paint a fully red crown or a broad black face mask (Eurasian Green Woodpecker); only the male's forecrown is red.
Do not paint black-and-white pied plumage or a red vent (Great Spotted Woodpecker, Dendrocopos major).
Do not paint spots, bars or streaks on the underparts; they are plain.
Do not give the female any red.
